title: ShopFlow Checkout Intermittent Payment Failures After Infrastructure Change
description: Starting around 14:10 UTC, ShopFlow customers began experiencing intermittent checkout failures. Customers report that some orders complete successfully while others remain stuck on 'Processing' for 20-40 seconds before returning HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout. The checkout-service shows elevated latency and the API gateway reports an increase in 504 responses. payment-service also shows increased request latency, but CPU and memory utilization remain within normal limits. The incident began approximately 12 minutes after a deployment to payment-service. No application code changes were made to checkout-service or order-service during this period. Database CPU is approximately 48%, database connections are below the configured maximum, and Redis memory utilization is normal. The payment team reports that payment requests occasionally take significantly longer than normal. A network connectivity check between checkout-service and payment-service shows no packet loss.

Payment Service Deployment Change - 2026-07-26
Deployment: payment-service version 2026.07.26-3 at 14:08 UTC.
Changes: Payment provider client library upgraded from version 4.8.1 to 5.1.0. Default HTTP request timeout changed from 3 seconds to 10 seconds. Connection pool configuration was unchanged.
No changes were made to checkout-service, order-service, PostgreSQL, Redis, or API Gateway.

Payment Provider Integration Investigation:
Normal payment authorization latency: 150-400 ms.
Observed latency after 14:10 UTC: 4-8 seconds.
Provider-side health: Healthy.
Network connectivity: Healthy.
Observed behavior: The new payment client library waits for an extended period when the provider response is delayed. The checkout-service has a request timeout of 5 seconds. Therefore, payment-service requests can remain active beyond the checkout-service timeout.

evidence.source_name: Knowledge Base Document - ShopFlow Checkout Timeout Runbook
evidence.content:
ShopFlow Checkout Timeout Runbook:
When checkout-service communicates with payment-service, checkout-service has a downstream request timeout of 5 seconds. If payment-service takes longer than 5 seconds to return, checkout-service terminates the request and the API Gateway may return HTTP 504.
When investigating checkout 504 errors, do not automatically assume database or checkout-service failure. Check: 1. payment-service latency 2. downstream dependency latency 3. recent payment-service deployments 4. timeout configuration 5. network connectivity 6. database connection utilization.
A healthy database with normal CPU and connection utilization makes database connection-pool exhaustion less likely. If payment-service latency increases immediately following a payment-service deployment, investigate changes to the payment client, timeout behavior, retry configuration, and connection handling.

Resolved Incident INC-2026-041: Checkout 504s caused by payment dependency latency.
Affected Service: payment-service.
Root Cause: Payment client timeout configuration caused downstream requests to exceed checkout timeout.
Symptoms: HTTP 504 responses, Checkout latency increase, Payment authorization latency increase.
Resolution: Corrected payment client timeout configuration, aligned downstream timeout with checkout timeout, deployed corrected configuration.
Evidence: Payment latency increased after deployment, Database remained healthy, Network connectivity remained healthy.
Confidence: 94%
